Although this time the spotlight was stolen by the iOS 27 public beta, Apple also released a new public beta firmware for AirPods this week. This update brings a long-awaited feature to supported AirPods models: custom EQ.

AirPods Public Beta Details

The AirPods public beta firmware version is 9.0.314, with build number 9A314b. The following AirPods models are eligible for this update:

  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2 (Lightning and USB-C versions)
  • AirPods 4
  • AirPods 4 (Active Noise Cancellation version)
  • AirPods Max 2

You can opt into the AirPods public beta within the "Settings" app on your iPhone. When your AirPods are connected, you will see a toggle in the "Settings" app to enable the beta firmware. After that, as long as your AirPods are in their charging case and within range of the paired iPhone, the beta will automatically download and install.

  • Open the "Settings" app
  • Tap "Bluetooth"
  • Tap the (i) next to your AirPods
  • Scroll down and turn on "AirPods Beta Updates"

Custom EQ Feature Lands on AirPods

After installing the AirPods public beta, you will discover a long-awaited new feature in the "Settings" app: custom EQ.

Thanks to the newly added custom EQ controls, you can now fine-tune your AirPods' sound more precisely. Within the "Settings" app, you can manually adjust the bass, mid, and treble of your AirPods.

Apple explains: "AirPods are meticulously crafted by Apple's design and engineering teams to faithfully reproduce the original sound of music, TV shows, movies, and even calls. If you prefer a different sound style, you can also customise how your AirPods present any audio they play."

While adjusting custom EQ settings, you can directly play songs from Apple Music within the "Settings" app to hear the effects of your adjustments in real time.

This feature is by no means the most advanced equaliser functionality—it's just a basic three-band system. However, for AirPods users, this is a long-awaited feature that Apple has finally delivered—even though most people will likely stick with the default settings.

You can find this brand-new custom EQ feature under the "Audio & Routing" menu for your AirPods in the "Settings" app. All AirPods equipped with the H2 chip can use it, including AirPods Pro 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods 4, and AirPods Max 2.

Other New Features iOS 27 Brings to AirPods

Below are other new features iOS 27 brings to AirPods:

  • Redesigned Settings App: Within iOS 27, Apple has redesigned the AirPods interface in the "Settings" app. Controls have been reorganised, separating features like hearing health, "Find My," and Live Translation into individual menus.
  • Adaptive Audio Slider: Within the "Settings" app, you can now use a slider to more precisely adjust Adaptive Audio mode.
  • GymKit: Although GymKit has been available for several years, it has always required pairing with an Apple Watch. As my colleague Zac mentioned, iOS 27 brings the full GymKit experience to iPhone and AirPods Pro 3.
  • Precision Finding: You can use the Precision Finding feature within the "Find My" app on your Apple Watch to locate your AirPods Pro 3.
  • Siri AI: When paired with a supported iPhone, AirPods can interact with Siri AI.

Wrapping Up

Which new AirPods feature are you most looking forward to trying? Will you give the new custom EQ feature a go? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
